account: This morning I read today's appointment book at the office. I am due here at 08:00, at the east-bank mill for a grain inspection at 10:00, home for lunch, back for council letters at 13:00, at the neighbour's east-dock cottage for tea at 15:00, and in the office at 16:30 for Builder's findings. Builder has approached early about the preventive inspection I authorized yesterday for two emeralds total. He reports no visible bridge defects and says the entrance door works normally; no confirmed safety problem has been brought to me. The unusual feature is that he still asks which landing to inspect, although I told Secretary last night to specify the east ferry landing and she acknowledged recording it. I do not know why that clarification has not reached him. He also lacks a writing book or funds and asks whether Secretary can transcribe his findings for his review within the agreed fee. This appears to be an effort to settle the scope and practical reporting arrangements, not evidence of an emergency. The inspection is intended to check town hall doors, bridge decking, and the east ferry landing; repairs and extra charges remain unauthorized.
